The two document-layout idioms (L5 'Under that went her name and her rank', L351 'The same hook came again and again down the column') give no revision or cognition verb to a receiver noun. secondSweepP5P6.bodyPartSubjects: Seven were found, and each one is involuntary, a state or perceptual: L9 'His pen hand shook' is a tremor. L29 'her jaw shut so hard that a muscle jumped' is an absolute state with an involuntary muscle. L173 and L343 fingertips going white is blanching. L303 'The fingers Tam had bitten caught the edge late and held badly' is an injured grip, and the injury is the point. L329 'Her elbow moved on the slates' is an accidental slip that sets off the grit run. L379 'her fingertips pressing white' is an absolute with blanching. L297 'the boots went off to the left' is perceptual, because she can only see his boots through the spokes. None of them says found, knew, carried or settled.
secondSweepP5P6.metaphorChains: None. The staff takes four separate literal physical verbs in four different paragraphs (took her weight, knocked on the cobbles, the knock came down the street, the heel ground on the floor). That is not a chain of human verbs.
